tail.title: Operating Multi-Node Full Fine-Tuning on NVIDIA B300: A Field Report on Telemetry-Based Triage, Negative Results, and Operational Hardening
tail.summary: Full fine-tune of Qwen3-32B on 16x B300 across two nodes with FSDP/ZeRO-3, claiming no new algorithm and delivering practitioner artifacts instead. A power-draw triage table distinguishes compute, communication, data starvation, checkpoint/deadlock and idle by board wattage - necessary because utilization reads 100% during an NCCL hang. The negative results dispel folklore: a controlled A/B found per-step NFS reading matches a pretokenized local cache (~53k tok/s) because the corpus fits in page cache, and an earlier 'throughput collapse' was NFS/CPU contention, not storage. Plus 4/8/16-GPU strong-scaling numbers and a worked epoch-end NCCL deadlock.

tail.title: Hyper-ES: Effective Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning via Descent Direction Merging
tail.summary: Evolution strategies fail on billion-parameter LLMs because in that dimensionality nearly all random perturbations are orthogonal to useful update directions. Hyper-ES first runs a few cheap gradient-based fine-tunes to obtain descent directions whose span forms a compact adaptation subspace, then applies CMA-ES to optimize layer-wise DARE-TIES merging coefficients within that subspace - searching over combinations of meaningful directions rather than arbitrary full-model noise. Tested on three Qwen2.5-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill backbones.

tail.title: PRISM: Priority-aware Rubric Internalization via Structured Multimodal Data Synthesis
tail.summary: Inverts the usual rubric setup: instead of the model being scored against a rubric, it is the executor that must verify each typed, prioritized rule before issuing an overall judgment. The four-stage synthesis pipeline produces persona-task pairs, prefix-guided rule sets, quality-filtered rubrics and structured verification traces, and PRISM-Eval uses deterministic matching against fixed labels so no inference-time judge is needed. 10K synthesized samples lift Qwen3-VL-4B from 9.5% to 30.1% Strict accuracy while preserving general benchmark performance, transferring to four other open MLLMs.

tail.title: FinReportBench: Measuring and Improving Institution-Grade Financial Report Generation
tail.summary: A 35-item rubric derived through expert partial orders, multimodal evidence and audits of decision boundaries, covering deliverability, report identity and institutional completeness, applied to 244 bilingual tasks curated from 10,000 balanced Chinese and English financial-research records with the public query, reconstructed trajectory and hidden source packet separated. Three independent judge families reproduce the expert partial order at near-ceiling rates, evidence that bounded observable criteria support reliable LLM judging. Across nine model families basic deliverability is nearly saturated while report identity and institutional completeness remain the bottleneck.

tail.title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization
tail.summary: Per-user adapters and user-conditioned reward models both suffer data sparsity and generalize badly to unseen users. In-context learning leaves context influence uncontrolled; Context Steering applies a fixed coefficient and costs two forward passes per token. CCS adds a lightweight adapter on a frozen backbone that decides per token whether and how strongly user context should affect generation, learned from an oracle context-conditioned LM and defaulting back to the base model when context is unhelpful. A single adapter trained on one dataset improves quality in-domain and on four OOD personalization benchmarks.

tail.title: Not Every Divergence Should Be Suppressed: Counterfactual Recoverability in On-Policy Distillation
tail.summary: Divergence-based on-policy distillation cannot tell whether an erroneous prefix is still correctable. This replays each error state through budget-matched teacher-continuation and rollback branches and labels states recoverable, irreversible-but-avoidable, or ambiguous. On AIME diagnostics the mean continuation-minus-rollback effect is 0.185 for recoverable states and -1.000 for irreversible ones - opposite intervention preferences. A branch-derived recoverability proxy achieves AUC 1.000 against 0.392 for divergence alone, and recoverability-aware control reaches 0.578 on held-out AIME2025 versus 0.517 for the best baseline.

tail.title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture
tail.summary: AI agents that sign commits, authenticate API calls or issue certificates keep private keys in plaintext files, environment variables or container memory, readable by any process with sufficient privileges - and a recent production incident exfiltrated keys from a widely deployed framework via email injection in under five minutes. The proposal moves keys into hardware (HSM, TPM, smart card) behind a vendor-neutral PKCS#11 interface so the host only ever receives results via opaque handles, wrapped in a five-layer zero-trust stack and evaluated against 12 injection scenarios derived from AgentDojo.

tail.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
tail.summary: An agent's capability depends on the harness - prompts, tools, control flow, memory, orchestration code - as much as on weights, yet there is no protocol for measuring how well models improve a harness. HarnessOpt-Bench gives an optimizer LLM a target agent's seed harness, graded evaluation feedback and a fixed evaluation budget under expensive stochastic evaluation, scoring its final nominated candidate by normalized gain over the seed on an inaccessible held-out partition. A trusted execution environment enforces the evaluation boundary, meters target-agent resource use and preserves candidate versions for audit. Five frontier LLMs evaluated.

tail.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents
tail.summary: Rewarding only final-answer correctness or intermediate progress never checks whether post-retrieval actions are actually grounded in what was retrieved, which encourages prior-driven reasoning: the agent concludes from internal knowledge and uses retrieval to confirm it. CIPO assigns dense turn-level credit to reasoning actions demonstrably influenced by retrieved information and combines that evidence-use signal with a global outcome reward, explicitly targeting confirmation bias rather than accuracy.

tail.title: CohortHijack: Robustness of Single Cell Annotation to Companion Cell Removal
tail.summary: A target-preserving attack surface nobody was looking at: many single-cell annotation tools refine a label using nearby cells or cluster voting, so removing other cells from the query cohort can flip the target's label without touching the target profile, base prediction, or model. On PBMC3K and Paul15, multi-start search changed 24.33% of linear-SVM targets and 19.67% of logistic-regression targets while removing a small fraction of the cohort and keeping mean collateral change under 0.4%. The effect vanished when neighbourhood refinement was disabled, and CellTypist's refined labels also shifted after small removals.

tail.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
tail.summary: Fixed-budget agent comparisons either keep paying after the result is settled or stop too early, and naive optional stopping with an ordinary confidence interval voids the stated level. AIVAT's conditional mean-zero corrections cut variance by a median 54x across 15 LLM agent configurations over 71,439 paired heads-up no-limit hold'em hands but do not say when to stop. Combining it with continuously monitored confidence sequences, at nominal 95% and +/-1 big blind precision, raw outcomes need a median 74x as many hands to stop as AIVAT-corrected ones. A transferable pattern for any expensive paired model comparison.

tail.title: Vibe Compiler: A Research-Logic Synthesis Tool That Runs without Prompt Engineering -Toward Enhancing Metacognition for Sustaining Agency in the Age of Generative AI-
tail.summary: Frames generative AI's threat to epistemic agency as uncritical acceptance of AI-generated reasoning and proposes a Synthesis-Analysis Reciprocity Model where synthesis assembles an artifact and analysis constrains the next synthesis against objective indicators. The Vibe Compiler compiles vague research ideas against a paper ontology of sixteen academic parameters; compilation failures indicate missing logical components, and rather than autofilling them the system returns reflective questions. Structural gaps are characterised along cognitive function (synthesis vs analysis) and executing agent (human vs AI).

tail.title: Shaping Human-AI Interactions to Provide Improvement Pathways and Balance Competing Objectives
tail.summary: Thesis on the loop where people evaluated by an AI form beliefs about how it works, strategically present their attributes accordingly, and receive a decision back. Three goals in tension: help individuals form accurate beliefs so they can improve at minimal cost, encourage genuine improvement while discouraging gaming, and keep the system achieving its objective. Combines theoretical analysis, data-driven modelling, human-subject experiments and empirical evaluation from both the evaluated individual's and the system's perspective.

tail.title: Mixed Uncertainty in One View: Co-Visualizing Statistical Variability and Qualitative Confidence
tail.summary: Three preregistered human-subjects studies, total N=923, on how the presentation of experts' qualitative confidence alongside line-chart confidence intervals changes non-expert decisions. Experiment 1 replicates that showing qualitative confidence alongside statistical variability shifts decision patterns, now in the time-series line chart context. Experiments 2 and 3 compare separate encodings (text, icons) against integration into the interval itself via color, transparency and a blurred stroke, finding several non-textual encodings that work.

tail.title: IntentLint: Supporting Intent Scaffolding and Prompt-time Linting in Human-AI Collaborative Data Analysis
tail.summary: Targets the failure where shared-understanding artifacts in collaborative analysis go stale, leaving undocumented assumptions, cross-user misaligned intent, context-poor prompts and unwanted agent behaviour. IntentLint infers analytic intent from shared notebooks, represents it as structured editable rules, and checks each user's prompt against those shared rules before it reaches the agent. A study with 16 data analysts found it improves awareness of collaborators' intent and prompts reflection on analytic strategy.

tail.title: Preference-Driven Online Adaptation for Personalized Interaction Initiation in Proactive AI Assistants
tail.summary: Proactive assistants must decide when to interrupt, which is user-specific and unlearnable in advance, and the moments worth interrupting are sparse and scattered across fine-grained user states. EOPA grounds timing preferences in measurable contextual evidence through two carriers - temporal preference anchors and evidence-bearing activity prototypes - deriving evidence at each polling step via user-prior-smoothed estimation and uncertainty-guided scaling, then fusing it into an interact-or-stay-silent decision before generating a context-aware response from high-quality historical demonstrations.

tail.title: An entropic explanation of insistence on sameness in autism
tail.summary: Proposes insistence on sameness as constrained minimization of an entropy metric D_H(R,M) = H(R|M) + H(M|R), where R is a stream of random stimuli and M a memory storing them, with the conditional entropies read as surprise and uncertainty. The argument: to minimize the metric an individual can either learn about R or restrict R to what M already holds, and insistence on sameness is the second strategy. The framework is then used to quantify sensory overload, deprivation, anxiety, comfort zone and rigidity, and to derive care guidelines. Speculative theory, but the kind of formalization worth arguing with.

tail.title: Predicting Task Difficulty Without Rollouts
tail.summary: Forecasting an agent's success probability from a task description before running costly simulations, studied across 17 agentic benchmarks spanning coding, mathematics, ML, web navigation and function calling. The methodological warning is that AUC can mask poor difficulty estimates entirely. Token-level entropy emerges as a useful predictive signal, and residuals between expected and observed difficulty expose hidden environment flaws such as contamination and infeasible tasks - i.e. the error term is a benchmark-auditing instrument.

tail.title: Innovation-Residual Auditing of Autonomous Analysis Agents: Localization, Detection Limits, Error Control, and Identifiability
tail.summary: Analyses whether unsupervised audits of autonomous data-analysis agents - trained only on analyses known to be sound, flagging operations that depart from the model - can actually localize the operation that caused an error. The score choice decides everything: scoring each operation against only its immediate predecessor makes operations that merely inherit an earlier error indistinguishable from correct ones, so one mistake yields one flag, while scoring against a longer reconstruction smears a single mistake across many operations. Quantifies the spread and gives false-flag-rate control requiring only exchangeability of sound analyses.

tail.title: From Continuous Predictors to Clinical Thresholds: Early Evidence on Performance Trade-offs of Guideline-Based Categorisation for Ischaemic Stroke Outcome Prediction
tail.summary: Motivated by a clinician user study asking for guideline-aligned cut-offs, this replaces continuous predictors with clinically informed categorical encodings in 90-day ischaemic stroke outcome models on a multi-centre European registry stratified into three treatment cohorts. Fully categorised gradient-boosted models are statistically indistinguishable from continuous ones in two cohorts and significantly worse in one. Global feature importance rankings stay consistent, so discretising to guideline thresholds preserves the prognostic hierarchy - a rare quantification of the interpretability-accuracy trade a clinician actually asked for.

tail.title: Adversarial Attacks for Good: A Survey of Proactive Protection across the Visual Content Lifecycle
tail.summary: Maps five research communities that independently inverted adversarial perturbations into protective tools at different lifecycle stages: privacy filters against unwanted recognition at sharing time, unlearnable examples against unauthorized training, generative safeguards against malicious editing or imitation, adversarial CAPTCHAs for access control against automated agents, and provenance mechanisms for post-circulation attribution. Notes they were developed in separate venues with incompatible success criteria while all exploiting the same persistent gaps between human perception and machine interpretation.

tail.title: A Self-Explainable Deep Architecture for Security Applications
tail.summary: Argues post-hoc explanation methods for security models fail on three counts: reduced faithfulness from local approximation error, instability from reliance on randomness, and computational cost that rules out real-time use. XSec instead learns interpretable structure during training, using a mask-based approach to extract informative sub-features and learn class prototypes, then computing similarity against those prototypes in a dedicated layer at test time so explanations come from the forward computation itself. Evaluated across five security scenarios.

tail.title: HexMIL: Hierarchical Attention MIL for Ante-Hoc Explainable Detection of AI-Manipulated CT Volumes
tail.summary: Medical deepfake detectors generalize badly to unseen generators and offer no interpretability. HexMIL is mask-free, trained on binary volume-level labels only, decomposing each CT volume into a patch and slice hierarchy aggregated by independent gated attention modules whose weights combine into a full-resolution 3D attention volume localizing the manipulation without pixel-level annotation. The claim worth noting: unlike Grad-CAM, those attention weights are the exact forward computation driving the decision, making the spatial attribution structurally faithful rather than post-hoc. Tested cross-generator on M3DSynth and CT-GAN.

tail.title: Big, Bright, or Invisible: A Frozen-Feature Benchmark of 3D CT Foundation Models
tail.summary: Ten frozen CT encoders across three thoracic cohorts including an unseen internal clinical dataset, probed with kNN, zero-shot prompting and linear probing. There is no universal SOTA - rankings fluctuate substantially with evaluation context, and a lightweight supervised encoder stays competitive with vision-language-aligned foundation models. The dominant determinant of performance is not architecture but a physical bottleneck: detectability scales with a finding's contrast against surrounding tissue and its spatial extent, confirmed by controlled within-organ comparisons.

tail.title: Robust Context-Aware Detection of Malicious Instructions in Text
tail.summary: Frames indirect prompt injection defence as segmenting text into benign and malicious sentences, and notes no existing detector combines query-relative detection at the segment level with hardening against adaptive evasion realizable in agentic execution. Builds a context- and query-aware malicious-sentence classifier, then presents two adversarial training methods to harden it, the first being feature-space adversarial training with evasions approximated by projected-gradient optimization. Pairs with PromptShield Home and the hardware-keystore MCP paper as this week's agent-injection cluster.

tail.title: Can Open-Weight LLMs Produce Kernel-Verified Coq Proofs? A Pilot Study
tail.summary: Six open-weight models, 100 CoqStoq theorems drawn from real Coq projects, one attempt each at temperature 0, scored only if the Coq kernel accepts the proof - no partial credit, no judge. Gemma 4 verified 12/100, Llama 3.3 verified 8, DeepSeek Coder V2 Lite verified 1, and Qwen 3.5, Mistral Small 3.1 and GPT-OSS verified none. The 21 successful model-theorem results covered 15 distinct theorems, 11 of which standard Coq tactics could not solve. Every verified theorem had a short or medium human reference proof.

tail.title: MoCA: Implicit Social Context Analysis
tail.summary: Formalizes implicit social communication along three dimensions - affection, intent, stance - with a benchmark of 3,108 multimodal instances from real-world sources carrying fine-grained cognitive annotations of who expresses what toward whom, and how and why it is conveyed. State-of-the-art multimodal LLMs struggle badly because they lean on explicit cues and cannot reason over latent social context. The proposed method is conflict-driven abductive reasoning. A rare benchmark that annotates the pragmatic mechanism rather than just the label.

tail.title: FOCUS: Decoupling Expert Personas in LLMs to Enhance Domain Expert Capabilities
tail.summary: Activating an expert persona improves domain accuracy, but existing persona control suffers cross-domain coupling that produces overly aggressive behaviour in high-caution domains like healthcare and excessive conservatism in risk-sensitive ones like trading. FOCUS extracts expert persona vectors automatically, applies orthogonal decomposition to decouple them by domain, and adds an expert gating module that activates personas by task context, trained in two stages with a gated selection regularizer. Evaluated on financial, legal, medical and cross-domain tasks. Directly relevant to anyone using persona conditioning as an experimental manipulation.

tail.title: Reading Between the Frames: Interpreting Implicit and Non-literal Meaning in Social Media Videos
tail.summary: DrivelHub+ collects 1,000 social media videos that appear nonsensical on the surface but carry deliberate pragmatic meaning, each annotated with a human-written implicit narrative explanation. Models are tested two ways: explanation, where they must articulate the pragmatic comprehension in natural language, and representation, adapting reasoning-as-retrieval to check whether model representations encode the implicit meaning at all. A much harder target than recognition or description benchmarks, and one where surface captioning gets you nowhere.

tail.title: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
tail.summary: Replaces open-ended multimodal reasoning after each GUI action with supervised structured prediction over explicit transition specifications and paired visual evidence, trained through SFT, teacher-student distillation and preference/reward refinement. The resulting 8B model reaches 82.16% transition-level accuracy on AndroidWorld, 11.83 points above zero-shot GPT-5.2 under identical structured input, wins online task success in three of four agent configurations, and cuts paid API charges in all four - a locally deployable substitute for repeated frontier-model reflection.

tail.title: Unified Agent: Managing Interactions across Devices
tail.summary: Argues that a cross-device, cross-time agent needs a compact carried state organizing engagement evidence, stated facts and the standing request, because a single agent treating devices as tools has no state management across time and multi-agent systems coordinate without maintaining that state. Builds a benchmark of user-agent interaction across devices and moments and significantly outperforms adaptations of four published designs, holding across MLLM family, capability and reasoning-mode changes.

tail.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
tail.summary: Replaces human preference annotation with dependency-parser supervision, converting parser judgements into preference pairs for delta-DPO, combining parser quality with lexical diversity in a composite reward, filtering low-information pairs by reward gap, and monitoring for reward hacking. On GPT-SW3-1.3B, Danish parse success rises from 69.0% to 93.8%, Icelandic gains +4.5 points on an independent Stanza evaluation with native speakers preferring SAGA outputs in 80% of pairwise comparisons, and Norwegian Bokmal improves by +28 points.

tail.title: Beyond Sequence Order: Syntax-Informed Positional Embeddings for Transformers
tail.summary: Learns a lightweight syntactic prior from dependency parses during pretraining and injects it across absolute, relative and rotary positional embedding families for both encoders and decoders, leaving self-attention untouched. Where the prior should enter depends on architecture: autoregressive decoders with relative PE do best when the prior is coupled multiplicatively with the relative-position term of the attention score, while encoders do best adding it directly to input embeddings. Improves SyntaxGym by up to 10.3% while simultaneously cutting perplexity 9.0%.

tail.title: The Order Is the Guarantee: Verifier-Budgeted Code Deletion with Static-First Learned Proposals
tail.summary: Starts from the observation that prompt-driven coding is additive - branches, guards and fallbacks accumulate faster than obsolete logic is removed - and studies the inverse problem under finite execution-verification capacity. Redundant-code reduction becomes proposal scheduling: a ranker orders single-statement deletion candidates, the test suite accepts the first that passes, a budget bounds how many get tested. The claim is that candidate order, not model confidence, is the control surface a deployment can reason about. DELSCOUT's five-slot schedule (three deterministic shortest-first, two learned) raises verified-deletion coverage 9.5% relative across nine MBPP replications with 0.5B, 0.6B and 8B rankers.

tail.title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
tail.summary: Quantifies where coding-agent tokens actually go: on SWE-Bench Verified a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, much of it grep, glob and view_file. A 14B retrieval agent trained end-to-end with GRPO preserves resolve rate (27.0% vs 25.8% no-retrieval) with 15% fewer rounds and 19% fewer tokens. The transferable finding is a precision threshold for downstream utility: BM25 at 0.375 precision degrades the agent, Jina at 0.445 is neutral, CodeGrep at 0.677 crosses into reducing rollout cost.

tail.title: EviGraph: Evidence-Guided Autonomous Research Agents
tail.summary: Autonomous research agents produce unsupported claims and inconsistencies between question, experiment, result and conclusion because sequential pipelines never maintain or validate the evolving claim-evidence structure. EviGraph makes a typed evidence graph - Problem, Gap, Hypothesis, Experiment, Finding, Claim - the operational state of the agent rather than a post-hoc record, inspecting chains for missing dependencies and result-claim inconsistency, localizing the earliest weak node and regenerating its downstream subgraph. Manuscripts are only generated once every retained claim is grounded in a validated chain.

tail.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
tail.summary: RP-OPSD guides privileged distillation toward reasoning pivots - decisions that advance or redirect the reasoning process - using the distributional shift between matched teacher views with and without an English reference solution as the operational proxy, across 17 languages and multiple difficulty levels. Worth flagging that at least six near-identical on-policy self-distillation variants (SPOT, OCSD, SMRC-SD, DASH, AgentOPSD, RP-OPSD) landed in a 48-hour window, all attacking the same credit-assignment gap from slightly different angles - a sign the subfield is saturating.

tail.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
tail.summary: Critic-free turn-level credit assignment that aggregates token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps into turn-level evidence and recursively updates a Bayesian belief state in log-odds space, converting sparse outcome supervision into turn-level credit and identifying pivotal turns by marginal belief revision between consecutive states. Compatible with standard policy optimization, needing no extra critic or rollouts. On ALFWorld, WebShop and Search-QA with Qwen2.5 at 3B and 7B it beats GRPO and strong self-distillation baselines, reaching 89.1% success on ALFWorld.

tail.title: Claude Managed Agents get hard session budgets with a budget_reached stop reason
tail.summary: You can now cap a Claude Managed Agents session's spend at public list rates; when the cap is hit the session pauses with a new budget_reached stop reason instead of issuing further model requests, and changing or removing the budget resumes it. Deployments accept the same budget parameter and apply it to every session they start. Relevant if you run long-horizon agent sessions and want a hard ceiling rather than post-hoc billing surprises.

tail.title: bartowski ships imatrix GGUFs of BTL-4 the day after release
tail.summary: Standard bartowski llama.cpp imatrix quant set for the 35B BTL-4 agentic model, Apache 2.0, tagged image-text-to-text. The base card's own llama.cpp invocation uses BTL-4-IQ2_XXS with q8_0 K/V cache at 32K context, which is the configuration that gets a 35B MoE onto a single consumer card. Note the card's warning that reasoning must be separated from content (--reasoning-format deepseek on llama.cpp) or the model repeats turns instead of terminating.

tail.title: BTL-4 gets a ROCm FP4 Strix Halo GGUF build for Ryzen AI Max iGPUs
tail.summary: A Q4_0 / ROCm-FP4 GGUF conversion of BTL-4 targeted specifically at gfx1151 Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max) parts, tagged moe + vision + llama-cpp. Part of a small but growing pattern of quants cut for AMD unified-memory laptops rather than discrete NVIDIA cards. Same-day companion to the bartowski build; no independent benchmark numbers are published for the quantized weights.

tail.title: BigBang-V1 claims a 35B beats DeepSeek V4 Pro (1.6T) on four frontier benchmarks
tail.summary: An Apache-2.0 post-train of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using an adversarial generator/critic loop that synthesised roughly 10,000 high-difficulty verifiable examples. The card claims aggregate performance between DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B) and V4 Pro (1.6T), and specifically claims it exceeds V4 Pro Preview on FrontierScience Research, Humanity's Last Exam, PaperBench Code-Dev and BioMysteryBench-HD. Extraordinary claims from a small unknown org with self-reported numbers and no third-party replication; a bartowski GGUF build appeared the same day, so it is at least cheap to test yourself.

tail.title: Wan-Animate-2 weights land: end-to-end character animation with no intermediate motion extractor
tail.summary: Alibaba's Wan team released Wan-Animate-2 inference code plus base and distilled 14B weights on 7 August under Apache 2.0, alongside Diffusers-format repos and a Comfy-Org packaging. It consumes driving video directly in a redesigned DiT rather than going through a pose/motion extractor, adds text-driven viewpoint control decoupled from the driving camera, and ships a Lite variant targeting real-time streaming latency. Paper is arXiv 2608.06009; ComfyUI and DiffSynth-Studio integrations are marked done.

tail.title: LiquidAI publishes eight MLX precisions of LFM2.5-2.6B, from 1.46GB mxfp4 to 5.02GB bf16
tail.summary: Liquid pushed a full MLX matrix for its 2.6B edge model on 6 August: bf16 (5.02GB), 8bit (2.67GB), mxfp8 (2.59GB), 6bit (2.04GB), 5bit (1.76GB), nvfp4 (1.53GB), 4bit (1.47GB) and mxfp4 (1.46GB, group size 32). 131072 context, hybrid conv+attention backbone, 16 languages, LFM 1.0 licence (not OSI-open). Apple-Silicon-only, but the size table is a useful reference for what a 2.6B costs at each format.

tail.title: lmstudio-community mirrors LFM2.5-2.6B as GGUF and four MLX bit-widths
tail.summary: LM Studio's community org published a GGUF build plus 4/5/6/8-bit MLX conversions of LiquidAI's LFM2.5-2.6B on 5 August, which is what makes the model one-click installable inside LM Studio rather than a manual download. Downloads are still small (tens to low hundreds), so this is availability news rather than adoption news.

tail.title: Kimi-K3-Cubic-2.5Bit: 2.8T params at an audited 2.4986 bits, one 8xH200 node
tail.summary: First public showcase of 'Cubic' quantization: parameterised non-uniform levels per weight group that relax the usual need for tiny group sizes (most layers here use group size 512). Mixed W2/W3/W4 expert weights give an audited effective width of 2.4986 bits, fitting Kimi K3 with ~700K context onto a single 8xH200 node at 57 tok/s single-request decode and 800-900+ tok/s at 64-way concurrency without speculative decoding. Fully data-free export with the converter script included; runs through QuantTrio's vLLM Cubic fork. Reported loss is groupwise NRMSE, not downstream task accuracy, which the card states plainly.

tail.title: LFM2.5-8B-A1B OptiQ 4-bit ships with an actual six-benchmark capability score
tail.summary: Sensitivity-driven mixed-precision quant of Liquid's sparse MoE (24 layers, 32 experts, 4 active): 5.46GB on disk down from 15.8GB bf16, 128K context, 60 of 66 fused expert projections at 4-bit with 6 kept at 8-bit. Unusually for a quant repo it publishes measured scores: MMLU 46.1%, GSM8K 54.6%, IFEval strict 32.9%, BFCL-V3 simple 24.5%, HumanEval pass@1 14.0%, HashHop long-context retrieval 0.0%, mean 28.69. The zero on long-context retrieval is the honest headline.

tail.title: mlx-community quantizes the DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5 distills at 4B and 9B
tail.summary: Eight MLX conversions (4bit/6bit/8bit/bf16 at both 4B and 9B) of Jackrong's DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5 distillations, converted with mlx-vlm 0.4.4 and keeping the multimodal processor config so image and video inputs still work. Tagged coder/agent/tool-use/long-context. These are third-party distills carrying a frontier lab's name in the repo id, not DeepSeek releases, and no evaluation of the distillation is published.

tail.title: Neural Drive: a 131M diffusion world model turned into a playable racing game, quantized to 86MB
tail.summary: OptiQ's mixed 4/8-bit build of codelion/neural-drive-model drops the weights from 523MB to 86MB. A 131M-parameter LatentDiT (dim 768, depth 12, patch 3) generates every frame of a racing game at 384x192 from the last 7 frames plus a 6-dim action vector, rectified flow distilled to a fixed 2-step sampler, over 10fps on an M3 Max. Training data came from SuperTuxKart via pystk with a deliberately bad driver so braking and drift appear in-distribution. Ships as a hidden `optiq game` easter egg; also runs in-browser on WebGPU.

tail.title: OptiQ 4-bit quants land for BTL-4, Macaw, LFM2.5-2.6B and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
tail.summary: A batch of mixed-precision Apple Silicon quants published on 6 August: BTL-4-OptiQ-4bit (the 35B agentic MoE), Macaw-OptiQ-4bit (LFM2 agent/tool-calling), LFM2.5-2.6B-OptiQ-4bit, LFM2.5-1.2B-JP-202606-OptiQ-4bit, Tiny-Pickle-v3-Coder-4bit and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-OptiQ-2bit. All served through `optiq serve`, which exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints with mixed-precision KV cache, tool-call healing and prompt caching, and auto-enables SSD expert streaming for MoEs that will not fit in RAM.

tail.title: prithivMLmods distills Opus reasoning traces into Qwen3.5 2B and 4B
tail.summary: Two Apache-2.0 multi-stage SFT runs on Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B trained on roughly 6,000 coding and STEM Opus reasoning traces plus additional reasoning data, with GGUF builds published alongside. 32K context, bf16, aimed at local inference. The card labels them experimental with possible reasoning artifacts and publishes no benchmark table, so treat the 'Opus-distilled' framing as a description of the training data source rather than evidence of transferred capability.

tail.title: DevQuasar GGUF-quantizes LG's K-EXAONE 2.0 750B-A37B and 236B-A23B
tail.summary: GGUF conversions of LG AI Research's two K-EXAONE 2.0 MoE flagships appeared over 5-6 August, following LG's own FP8, NVFP4 and DSpark variants which were themselves refreshed on 7 August. At 750B total / 37B active these are datacenter-scale even quantized; the 236B-A23B build is the more plausible target for a large local rig. No perplexity or KLD receipts are published for either quant set.

tail.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B gets a GGUF build
tail.summary: A quantized GGUF conversion of Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B, one of the few genuinely small new base models to surface this window. At 3B a Q4-class GGUF sits comfortably under 2.5GB, so it runs alongside other workloads on a 16GB card. The DevQuasar repo carries no evaluation of the quantization and the upstream model card is the only source of capability claims.

tail.title: bartowski quantizes gemma-4-31B-it-scotoma-2 with text, image and audio input
tail.summary: Llama.cpp imatrix quants of ReadyArt's 31B Gemma 4 finetune, built against llama.cpp b10262. The card confirms 31B parameters, text + image + audio input via the mmproj file, imatrix yes, MTP no. Multimodal GGUF with audio is still comparatively rare, so this is a usable local any-to-any target if you can live with a low-bit 31B.

tail.title: Unsloth republishes Ideogram 4 as an ungated mirror, with a loading trap documented
tail.summary: Unsloth mirrored ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-fp8 and -nf4 without the Hub gate, weights unmodified, under Ideogram's non-commercial licence. The card carries a genuinely useful warning: the repo keeps Ideogram's fused attention.qkv/attention.o layout, so a plain diffusers from_pretrained silently random-initialises the attention weights and emits garbage rather than raising. Use the -nf4-diffusers repo or a loader that splits the fused QKV. Ideogram 4 is a from-scratch text-to-image foundation model with a structured JSON prompting interface, not a FLUX finetune.

tail.title: FLUX.2 klein 4B base mirrored: undistilled, sub-second inference, 13GB VRAM
tail.summary: Unsloth mirrored Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 [klein] 4B Base under Apache 2.0, alongside klein-4B, klein-9B-ComfyUI, FLUX.2-dev, FLUX.2-VAE and the flux text encoders. The 4B Base is a rectified-flow transformer trained without step or guidance distillation, so it is the variant meant for LoRA training and fine-tuning rather than fastest sampling; BFL claims end-to-end inference under a second and operation from as little as 13GB VRAM. Commercial use permitted under Apache 2.0.

tail.title: Unsloth bulk-mirrors the local image-gen stack: Z-Image-Turbo, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, HiDream I1, Wan2.2-TI2V-5B GGUF
tail.summary: Over 6-7 August Unsloth published diffusers and ComfyUI-single-file mirrors for Z-Image-Turbo, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-2512, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, HiDream-I1 Full/Dev/Fast, Lumina-Image-2.0, SDXL base and turbo, plus a Wan2.2-TI2V-5B GGUF. No architectural changes - these are convenience republishes with matching ComfyUI packaging. Worth knowing about if you maintain a local ComfyUI/WAN stack and want one org to pull single-file checkpoints and text encoders from.

tail.title: drbaph converts the H3 Turbo LoRA for ComfyUI's pruned curve-form checkpoint
tail.summary: Third-party compatibility conversions of larryvrh's Turbo LoRA so it loads with ComfyUI's built-in MiniMax-H3 LoRA loader against the pruned/curve-form checkpoint, plus two further-trained checkpoint-500 variants. Ships both non-EMA (crisper, better at fast motion) and EMA (smoother but softer) weights in bf16, with an example workflow JSON. No retraining of the original distillation; credit and method belong to larryvrh.

tail.title: lightx2v releases its own MiniMax-H3 Turbo plus a Qwen3.6-27B prompt-rewriter LoRA
tail.summary: ModelTC published an Apache-2.0 MiniMax-H3 Turbo finetune covering t2v, i2v and r2v, plus a separate PEFT LoRA on Qwen3.6-27B that rewrites a short prompt into a structured H3 audio-video description (shot structure, camera motion, diegetic soundscape, non-diegetic music). Together they give a fully local pipeline: short prompt to rewriter to LightX2V inference with offloading, tensor/sequence parallelism and quantized checkpoints. The Turbo repo itself is a stub pointing at the ModelTC GitHub for reproduction.

tail.title: Sol-Attn sparse attention kernel packaged for the HF Kernel Hub
tail.summary: NVIDIA's Efficient-Large-Model org published Kernel Builder packaging for Sol-Attn, the sparse attention backend from NVlabs/Sana, pinned to commit 8a26fb0 and released Apache 2.0. Loadable with kernels.get_kernel("Efficient-Large-Model/Sol-Attn", version=1) and called as sol_attn(q,k,v,tau,thresh_type) over contiguous BF16 CUDA tensors with head dim 128. CUDA/Triton/CuTe-DSL. The only source change from upstream was converting internal imports to package-relative form.

tail.title: fal ships a sharded-state SGLang checkpoint for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Magic Prompt
tail.summary: An FP8 sharded-state SGLang artifact of a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B prompt-expansion model, published as a serving format rather than a new set of weights. Sharded-state checkpoints cut cold-start load time on multi-GPU serving, which is the whole point for a prompt rewriter sitting in front of an image pipeline. fal also published FlashPack-format builds of its Flux Vision Upscaler (T5XXL FP16 and SeedVR2 FP16) the same day.

tail.title: llama.cpp b10322: SYCL ssm_conv window-load coalescing gives 1.85x on Intel Arc
tail.summary: Coalescing the ssm_conv window loads in the SYCL backend nearly doubles that op on an Arc Pro B70 (97.68 to 52.95 us/run at n_t=512, 516 to 276 us at n_t=934, both about 1.85x). End-to-end that is a smaller 1.8-2.2% prefill gain on Qwen3.5 27B Q4_K_M with 48 of its 64 blocks using ssm_conv, and token generation is flat. The release notes publish the interleaved A/B methodology and rep counts, which is the standard llama.cpp holds itself to.

tail.title: llama.cpp b10321 fixes a silent Metal NORM/RMS_NORM correctness bug on partial simdgroups
tail.summary: ggml_metal_op_norm could size a threadgroup to a non-multiple of the simdgroup size, so the tail of the per-simdgroup partial sums was never read and the row mean and variance came out wrong for the whole row. At ne00_t=33 one of two partial sums was silently dropped. Fixed by rounding ne00_t up to a whole simdgroup rather than removing the clamp, which avoids inflating the threadgroup on 26 already-correct row lengths. No mainstream LLM hidden size hits this, but 320-channel norms in vision and audio towers do.

tail.title: llama.cpp adds an LRU scheduler to the server router and stops evicting busy models
tail.summary: Two router changes landed the same day: b10312 stops the multi-model router evicting a model that is currently serving requests, and b10313 adds an LRU scheduler with coalescing handling for requests leaving the waiting queue, plus tests and streaming support. Together they make llama-server's router usable as a real multi-model front end rather than something that thrashes under concurrent load. Relevant if you run several GGUFs behind one endpoint on a single GPU.

tail.title: ExLlamaV3 v1.4.0 adds DeepSeek V4 support and faster prefill across all models
tail.summary: turboderp's v1.4.0 adds DeepseekV4ForCausalLM support, improves AVX512 CPU offload performance, and speeds up prefill for every model, plus bug fixes and QoL work. ExLlamaV3's EXL3 quantization remains the main alternative to GGUF for people optimising single-GPU throughput on NVIDIA cards, so DeepSeek V4 architecture support is the practical unlock here. No headline throughput numbers are given in the release notes.

tail.title: vLLM cuts a v0.27.0 release candidate
tail.summary: v0.27.0rc1 was tagged on 7 August at commit 4b25076. The release body is empty, so there are no published highlights yet: the changes have to be read from the compare view against v0.26. Flagging it because vLLM minor bumps routinely carry architecture support and scheduler changes that break pinned deployments, and the two vLLM engineering blog posts from the same week (decode context parallelism, Blackwell disaggregated serving) point at what is landing.

tail.title: vLLM decode context parallelism claims 3x throughput on long-context agent workloads
tail.summary: DCP shards the KV cache across GPUs along the sequence dimension rather than the head dimension, which is what tensor parallelism does. vLLM reports 3x higher throughput than standard TP on long-context agentic workloads, where the KV cache rather than the weights is the memory bottleneck. This is a multi-GPU technique, so it is not directly usable on a single card, but it is the mechanism behind most of the long-context serving cost claims you will see quoted this month.

tail.title: vLLM reports 25K TPS/GPU on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4 with GB200 NVL72
tail.summary: A stacked-optimisation post: disaggregated prefill/decode serving on GB200 NVL72, Blackwell GDN kernels, HMA cache transfer, async scheduling fixes and srt-slurm recipes together reach 25K total tokens/sec per GPU on the NVFP4 build of Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Total TPS per GPU aggregates across concurrent requests, so this is a fleet-economics number, not a single-stream latency number, and it is on hardware essentially nobody outside a datacenter has.

tail.title: Unsloth v0.1.525-beta makes DSpark default and ships DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 dynamic GGUFs
tail.summary: DSpark support is now on by default with a claimed 2x faster inference. DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 dynamic GGUFs are published at UD-IQ1_S (83GB), UD-IQ3_XXS (104GB, fits a 128GB machine), UD-Q4_K_XL (155GB) and UD-Q8_K_XL (162GB, described as lossless); Kimi K3 spans UD-IQ1_S at 595GB to UD-Q8_K_XL at 1.56TB. Unsloth auto-detects multi-GPU setups and offloads layers to system RAM, and downloads now fall back to HTTP when XET stalls. The 2x claim is unbenchmarked in the notes.

tail.title: LocalAI 4.8.0 ships vllm.cpp, a Python-free C++20 inference engine measured at 1.045x vLLM
tail.summary: 386 PRs over 22 days. The headline is vllm.cpp (alpha): a C++20 engine that began as a vLLM port and now carries paged KV cache, continuous batching, prefix caching, scheduler and sampler with no Python, PyTorch or ggml at inference, loading both safetensors and GGUF and running on CPU, CUDA, Metal and Vulkan. Measured at 1.045x vLLM on Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4 at concurrency 1 with token-for-token identical output, and 1.5-2.2x on an M4 via the MLX GEMM provider. Also new: 3D generation as a first-class modality, a six-endpoint audio.cpp backend, per-node VRAM budgets, and a React bundle 3.48x smaller.

tail.title: LocalAI 4.8.2 adds a NeMo-Speech.cpp backend and gallery mirror fallback
tail.summary: Two quick follow-ups to 4.8.0. 4.8.1 fixed malformed GGUF metadata crashing VRAM estimation, restored the vllm-cpp ABI v10 mirror so the backend loads, and added Qwen3.5 9B HauhauCS and Defiant Fable gallery entries. 4.8.2 adds the NVIDIA NeMo-Speech.cpp backend and makes the model gallery default to index.localai.io with GitHub as a mirror plus a cached index fallback when the primary source fails.

tail.title: NVIDIA NeMo Speech 3.0: repo split, 800k lines of deprecated code deleted, uv-based installs
tail.summary: The first major release after NeMo split apart: this repo now covers only ASR, TTS, audio processing, speaker tasks and SpeechLM, with LLM, VLM, diffusion, export and evaluator collections moved to sibling repos under the NVIDIA-NeMo org. 800k lines of deprecated code removed, migration to uv, lighter containers, plus AGENTS.md and agentic skills. SpeechLM2 gains a NeMo Automodel backend (SALMAutomodel) with native LoRA and FSDP2/HSDP/TP/CP/EP parallelism, THD packed-sequence training, and encoder chunking for long audio. Note uv sync may replace Python/PyTorch/CUDA inside .venv.

tail.title: llama.vscode v0.0.59 introduces a scripting DSL for agent commands
tail.summary: Adds .lvs scripts: a simple DSL with variables, if/else and comments that can select or deselect models, agents and envs, change settings and run terminal commands. Scripts placed in the new scripts_folder show up under "/" in the agent prompt, with [p] marking commands that send a prompt and [s] marking ones that only execute a script. The stated plan is to reuse the same DSL for hooks later. Also more informative code-completion errors and a Telegram /chat command that works while the agent is running.

tail.title: FlashAttention 4 beta25 fixes a Blackwell sparse-MLA backward scatter bug
tail.summary: Five changes: SM100 functions removed from the Hopper FA3 path, a varlen dynamic persistent scheduler plus metadata for CuTe/SM100, a fix so sparse MLA backward no longer scatters dK/dV at -1 sentinel indices, a ROCm CK varlen_fwd binding argument fix, and a debug-methodology doc. The sentinel-index fix is a silent-corruption class bug in training, not a performance change.

tail.title: onnxruntime-genai cuts v0.15.1 and v0.15.2 on the same day
tail.summary: Two patch releases landed on 7 August with empty release bodies, so the contents have to be read from the commit range. onnxruntime-genai is the path most Windows-native and NPU-targeted local inference goes through (Copilot+ PCs, Qualcomm and Intel NPUs), so patch churn here affects on-device deployment rather than desktop GPU inference. Worth pinning rather than tracking latest given the same-day double bump.

tail.title: stable-diffusion.cpp cuts a master build after the LocalAI 4.8 sync
tail.summary: A rolling master build (813-bfbef5b) with no release notes; LocalAI pulled a subsequent commit c6beeef the following day as part of its 4.8.1 dependency sweep. stable-diffusion.cpp remains the ggml-based route to running diffusion models without a Python stack, which matters on machines where the ComfyUI dependency tree is the actual problem. Contents legible only from the commit log.

tail.title: Claude Code v2.1.224 adds self-hosted runners and cross-session agent messaging
tail.summary: `claude self-hosted-runner` turns your own machines or containers into a place Claude Code web, mobile and desktop sessions can run, on Team and Enterprise plans. Cross-session SendMessage lets sessions message each other across machines with ListAgents for discovery (macOS and Linux), gated by a new crossSessionInbound setting so messages into a bypassed-permissions session are held for approval. Also an `archive` plugin source installing from a zip over HTTPS with optional SHA-256 pinning, and sandbox credential-masking with JWT claim masking and AWS SigV4 re-signing.

tail.title: OpenAI Codex 0.147.0 adds portable agent plugins and opt-in MCP 2026-07-28 protocol
tail.summary: Installs portable Agent Plugins with search across local, personal, workspace and remote catalogs; adds persistent manually-ordered conversation sections; adds an --approve-for-me flag for automatically reviewed approvals; imports Cursor-managed skills and syncs changes to imported Claude and Cursor conversations without duplicating. Supports the opt-in MCP 2026-07-28 protocol including paginated discovery, multi-round requests and non-blocking server startup. Security fixes include redacting bearer tokens from displayed commands and replayed history, requiring explicit trust for unfamiliar local projects, and denying plugin network access when policy updates fail.

tail.title: Codex 0.146.1 backports safer automatic-review defaults for cyber-capable models
tail.summary: A single-purpose patch release: cyber-capable models get more conservative automatic-review defaults, and the terminal UI now explains permission changes when they happen rather than applying them silently. Backported from main as PR #37057. Worth noting as a data point on how frontier labs are handling capability-triggered policy inside their own coding agents.

tail.title: Gemini CLI ships v0.54.0 and v0.54.4 with HTTPS enforcement and session-ID rotation fixes
tail.summary: v0.54.0 landed 6 August and v0.54.4 on 7 August, with v0.55.0 previews and nightlies running alongside. Security-relevant changes include enforcing HTTPS for GoogleCredentialsAuthProvider to prevent cleartext credential leakage, explicit tag-length validation in the file keychain, and sanitising issue titles into untrusted_context. Also rotates the session ID on model fallback to avoid stateful API errors, and filters thought parts from history when context management is disabled.

tail.title: Cline 4.1.4 hard-blocks file-editing shell commands in plan mode
tail.summary: Cline removed model-initiated plan-to-act switching entirely, so leaving plan mode is now driven by the user rather than the model deciding mid-turn, and replaced prompt-level restraint with hard blocks: file manipulation, in-place editors, redirection to files, mutating git subcommands and package installs are refused in plan mode while read-only investigation still works. Also recovers from context exhaustion by compacting and retrying once, and retries empty model responses on every provider rather than only Ollama.

tail.title: Cline unifies reasoning-effort handling across AI SDK providers including Ollama
tail.summary: Across v4.1.5, v4.1.6, cli-v3.0.51 and sdk v0.0.71, Cline replaced per-provider thinking overrides with the AI SDK's native reasoning setting, so effort levels and explicit reasoning-off are honoured consistently wherever the provider supports them, Ollama included. The model catalog was refreshed from models.dev and meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor was added to the Cline provider. Error telemetry is now attributed to the model actually in use rather than the wrong one.

tail.title: Cline desktop 0.0.10 adds OAuth for remote MCP servers with pre-registered clients
tail.summary: Remote MCP servers can now authenticate via OAuth from Settings, with visible auth status, cancel/retry on a pending authorization, and support for servers requiring a pre-registered client ID/secret rather than dynamic registration; stored tokens are invalidated when a server's client config changes. MCP errors now surface on the individual server instead of a page-level banner, and a misconfigured server shows its error rather than vanishing from the list. Failed turns no longer fail silently.

tail.title: pydantic-ai 2.26.0 adds hidden tools revealed on demand, plus first-party run cancellation
tail.summary: Tools can now be hidden until revealed via tool search, load_capability or ToolReturn.tools, using each provider's native deferral channel rather than a framework-side simulation - directly relevant if you are hitting tool-count limits in large agent setups. Also adds AgentRun.cancel()/RunContext.cancel()/RunCancelled, promotes run_stream_events() to a public AgentRunEvents handle, adds Model.resolve_prompt_cache_retention(), and documents DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenAIResponsesModel. Fixes gate OpenRouter off native mid-conversation system messages.

tail.title: Meta's llama-stack is now 'ogx' - repo renamed and v1.3.0 adds a Meta remote inference provider
tail.summary: github.com/meta-llama/llama-stack now redirects to ogx-ai/ogx, and the SDK packages are ogx-client and ogx-client-typescript. v1.3.0 adds a Meta AI remote inference provider with injectable network/TLS config, a Neo4j vector provider, anthropic_count_tokens via translation on OpenAIMixin, and a shared SSE passthrough helper for Anthropic-compatible providers. It also strips a duplicate /v1 prefix in vLLM Anthropic message URLs and warns at startup when authentication is not configured. A rename this size will break pinned git dependencies.

tail.title: OpenRouter documents per-key credit limits and enterprise workspace budgets
tail.summary: Every API key can carry a credit limit with daily, weekly or monthly resets on all tiers including free, with requests past the limit rejected and remaining balance readable from GET /api/v1/key. Workspace budgets are Enterprise-only: USD caps over daily/weekly/monthly/lifetime windows, 403 at the limit, shorter windows must be smaller than longer ones, in-flight requests complete. The post also restates the fee structure: no markup on provider pricing, 5.5% on card top-ups with a $0.80 minimum, and 5% on BYOK model costs with the first 1M requests per month waived.

tail.title: LiteLLM cuts two v1.97.0 dev builds
tail.summary: Prerelease builds v1.97.0-dev.1 (5 August) and dev.2 (7 August). LiteLLM is the proxy layer most multi-provider billing and fallback logic runs through, so dev builds are where new model IDs and pricing tables land before the stable tag. Treat as a signal of what is about to be routable rather than something to deploy.

tail.title: LangChain ships langchain-openai 1.4.2 and langchain-anthropic 1.5.4
tail.summary: Two provider-package point releases in the window: langchain-anthropic 1.5.4 on 5 August and langchain-openai 1.4.2 on 7 August. Provider packages are versioned independently of core, so these are where new API surface (fast mode, effort ladders, mid-conversation tool changes) gets plumbed through. Neither carries a headline feature announcement.

tail.title: openai-agents-python v0.19.4 and crewAI 1.15.11/1.15.12
tail.summary: Routine point releases in two of the more widely deployed agent frameworks, both dated 5 August. Listed for completeness of the agent-framework release surface this window rather than for any headline capability; neither release carries a feature announcement in its notes.

tail.title: anthropic-sdk-typescript 0.116.0 plus five platform SDK bumps in one day
tail.summary: The core TypeScript SDK went to 0.116.0 alongside coordinated bumps of vertex-sdk 0.19.1, bedrock-sdk 0.32.1, google-cloud-sdk 0.0.7, foundry-sdk 0.4.1 and aws-sdk 0.6.2, all on 7 August. Simultaneous bumps across every cloud wrapper usually mean a shared API surface change landing at once - the same day the platform release notes added Managed Agents budgets, advisors and inference_geo.

tail.title: Ai2 releases TutorMoments: 462 real tutoring transcripts and 1,500+ teacher-annotated moments
tail.summary: An open replay-based evaluation framework testing whether an AI tutor knows when to help and when to hold back. TutorMoments-Preview is 462 de-identified text-only transcripts of real one-on-one maths tutoring with US students in grades 2-7, carrying more than 1,500 teacher-annotated key moments. Seven models were evaluated (Gemini 2.5 Pro and 3.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5 and 5.4 mini, DeepSeek V4 Pro). With plain prompts models over-help; an evaluation-aware prompt explaining the scaffolding-versus-rigour trade-off improves things substantially but still leaves them short of human tutors. Dataset on HF, eval code and model replay outputs on GitHub.

tail.title: ComfyUI v0.30.2 adds BFL Flux 3 video, Topaz Bloom 2 and Wonder 3.5, retires Kling legacy
tail.summary: A partner-node release rather than a core architecture change: Flux 3 video model support arrives via Black Forest Labs, plus Bloom 2 and Wonder 3.5 from TopazAI, while the retired Kling legacy models and their Virtual Try-On API are removed. The preceding v0.30.1 on 3 August was purely a frontend package bump to 1.47.12. All of these are hosted API nodes, so nothing here runs locally on your own GPU.

tail.title: Spaces: MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA demo and LFM2.5-2.6B running in-browser on WebGPU
tail.summary: akhaliq published a Space for the 4-step MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRA on 6 August, giving a zero-install way to check whether the plastic-skin artifacts the author warned about actually bite for your prompts. Alongside it, LiquidAI's LFM2.5-2.6B-WebGPU Space (4 August) runs the 2.6B edge model entirely client-side in the browser via WebGPU, no server inference. Both are useful triage tools before committing disk to weights.

tail.title: Why is everyone in tech so sad? Noema on a class of workers losing faith in the career
tail.summary: A long essay on what happens when an entire occupational class stops believing its career ladder exists - written about software, but the mechanism (a credential that no longer converts into security) is the one you are navigating between independent research and a funded PhD. 137 points and 224 comments on HN, with a comment section that is itself a data set on the mood.

tail.title: deltafin - full Kimi K3 as a single binary with an OpenAI-compatible server
tail.summary: A Rust binary that runs the uncompressed 2.8T Kimi K3 on one device with all 16 expert-routing layers live, nothing pruned. Streaming install starts at ~215 GB and fetches experts on demand rather than the full 1.7 TB. The genuinely useful part for your stack is the server design: it implements only the slice of /v1/chat/completions it can honour exactly and refuses unsupported requests instead of silently ignoring them - the opposite of the quiet-parameter-drop behaviour that has bitten large-N judge runs before.

tail.title: NIGHTRUN - boot your PC straight into an LLM, no operating system underneath
tail.summary: A UEFI-resident Rust runtime that boots from USB, loads a quantised model into RAM with CRC verification, seals storage so nothing can touch disk during generation, and gives you a framebuffer chat interface running CPU inference. Runs Llama 3.2 1B/3B, Granite 4.1 3B or Qwen3 4B in 4-8 GB, on x86_64 UEFI or a Raspberry Pi 5. Completely impractical and the purest expression of local-first there is - an afternoon's build with an installer that handles model conversion and flashing.

tail.title: local_bench - benchmark every model already installed on your machine, on your hardware
tail.summary: Discovers what you already have in Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible server and runs a live terminal leaderboard across four axes: tokens/sec and time-to-first-token, resident and peak memory, quality over 31 deterministic tasks, and joules per token if you give it root. pip install and run. The energy column is the unusual bit - it would tell you what a 5060 Ti actually costs you per judged item on a long PsychBench-style local run.

tail.title: super-simple-software-factory - deterministic Python owns the graph, agents are bounded nodes inside it
tail.summary: One skill you stamp into any repo (copy to .claude/skills/sssf, run install.py) that generates a workflow where Python controls sequencing, retries and acceptance gates while the agent only owns the work inside a single bounded phase - 'agent proposes, code disposes'. Phases pass typed JSON envelopes; every event streams to SQLite live so you can watch a run rather than replay it; a YAML roster lets you put a cheap model on extraction and an expensive one on judgement. This is close to the architecture your large-N pipelines already want.

tail.title: kaas - compile scattered notes, docs and transcripts into a Markdown wiki with no embeddings
tail.summary: Instead of chunking and embedding raw text, kaas runs a four-phase LLM pipeline - extract, classify, write, index - that compiles your material into human-readable, editable, version-controllable Markdown articles. It then exposes a single `ask` MCP tool to Claude Code that returns cited Markdown answers grounded in the compiled wiki. Docker or a shell installer, needs any OpenAI-compatible key. A compile-not-retrieve alternative worth benchmarking against your LKHS retrieval.

tail.title: Remembrane - agent memory in one SQLite file with exact recall and time travel
tail.summary: pip install remembrane, then store/recall/reinforce/forget against a single .db file you can copy, back up or commit. It scores every memory in one pass with hybrid vector plus BM25 rather than approximate nearest neighbour, so recall is complete rather than probabilistic, and every result explains its own score across similarity, recency decay, importance and learned usefulness. All mutations are journaled, so you can query what the agent knew at any past point. Deterministic by default, which means memory behaviour is unit-testable in CI.

tail.title: OptMem - permanent agent memory as a 426-token prompt plus one dependency-free Python file
tail.summary: Victor Taelin's minimal take: an append-only memory log organised into a binary tree, driven by three commands the agent learns from a 426-token block you paste at the top of your agent docs - `memo wake` at session start, `memo note` to record, `memo recall` / `memo zoom` to search or navigate. One Python 3 file at ~/.optmem/memo, no background processes, single disk seek at scale. The point is portability: the memory survives model changes, vendor switches and harness updates because it is just a file structure.

tail.title: swarm-forge - Uncle Bob's tmux orchestrator for a swarm of coding agents
tail.summary: Robert C. Martin has shipped a Clojure tool that runs a configured team of agents - coder, architect, cleaner, QA - each in its own git worktree so they cannot collide, communicating through validated message files rather than direct tmux commands. A swarmforge.conf declares topology and which backend each role uses; you pick a two-, four- or six-pack workflow and run ./swarm, and closing the first window shuts the whole swarm down. Notable mostly for who wrote it and how conventional the answer turned out to be.

tail.title: google/skills - Google's own agent skills for Cloud, BigQuery, Gemini API and GKE
tail.summary: Google has published a first-party skills repo covering Cloud onboarding and auth, BigQuery AI/ML, Gemini API integration, model tuning, prompt management and RAG engine work, plus GKE, databases, gcloud, monitoring and the six Well-Architected pillars. Installs with `npx skills add google/skills` or through the Claude Code plugin marketplace, and works across Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI. Mostly of interest as evidence that vendors now ship skills the way they used to ship SDKs.

tail.title: agentacct - a local dashboard for what your coding agents actually did and what it cost
tail.summary: Breaks each agent task into work steps - tools used, files changed, tests run, time and tokens spent - and renders it as a local-first dashboard instead of a raw token counter. Useful for the question you keep having to answer by hand: which stage of the NewsBrief run is eating the budget, the collectors or the synthesis.

tail.title: nativeprompt - rewrite a prompt into the native dialect of the model you are actually running
tail.summary: Takes a prompt and rewrites it according to each vendor's official prompting rules for the specific harness you are on (Claude Code versus Codex), and shows you which rule drove each individual edit rather than just handing back a rewrite. The per-edit attribution is the interesting part - it turns prompt porting into something you can inspect, which matters when you run the same rubric across models on OpenRouter and want to know whether a score gap is capability or phrasing.

tail.title: ponytail-improved - make your agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room
tail.summary: A skill built around one principle: the best code is the code you never wrote. It biases the agent toward deleting, reusing and refusing rather than generating, which is the correct default for a personal automation stack that already has more moving parts than you can hold in your head. Same author as ratchet and humanizer-cli, all zero-dependency.

tail.title: trace-file-lineage - find which script, notebook, command or agent produced a file
tail.summary: Works locally, returns evidence for its answer, and reports honest uncertainty when it cannot establish provenance. For a research repo where assets/stats has been regenerated by several different runs and at least one agent, this is the tool that answers 'which run produced this CSV' without you reconstructing it from timestamps.

tail.title: literature-review-agent - LangGraph pipeline for search, screening, outline and evidence-grounded writing
tail.summary: Four explicit stages - literature search, evidence screening, outline generation, then writing constrained to the screened evidence. The screening stage is the one that matters and the one most 'AI literature review' tools skip; worth reading as a structural comparison against your paper-library skill's title-verification-then-quote-backed-card approach.

tail.title: vetresearch-workbench - a domain research workbench with local RAG, bounded agents, citations and abstention
tail.summary: Veterinary medicine is incidental; the architecture is the point. Local RAG, agents with bounded tool use, auditable tool logs, mandatory citations, an explicit abstention path when evidence is insufficient, and a human review step. This is roughly the reference design for an evidence-grounded domain assistant, and abstention-as-a-first-class-output is exactly the axis your Explanation Gap work measures.

tail.title: career-ops - an open-source local job search that scores every posting on an A-F rubric
tail.summary: Scans job portals, evaluates each listing with a structured A-F rubric mapped to a 1.0-5.0 score, tailors your CV per application and tracks what you have sent - all running locally in your own agent rather than on someone's SaaS. The rubric-to-score step is the same machinery you build for judges, pointed at the thing you actually have to do this quarter.

tail.title: open-design - a local-first, open-source alternative to Claude Design where your coding agent is the design engine
tail.summary: A local desktop app that hands prototypes, landing pages, dashboards, slides and images to whichever coding agent you already run, instead of a hosted design product. Relevant for the parts of your output that are documents rather than code - brief.html, paper figures, and the decks that keep coming out of the consulting work.

tail.title: mcp-debug-proxy - a visual reverse proxy that shows you every MCP and OAuth message
tail.summary: Sits between your client and an MCP server and renders the actual traffic, including the OAuth handshake, in a visual timeline. The thing that makes MCP servers miserable to build is that failures are invisible - this is the tcpdump for that problem, and it is what you want open the next time mimesis or lkhs-memory silently returns nothing.

tail.title: plan-review - an independent second opinion on Claude Code plans before you approve them
tail.summary: Hooks the plan-approval step and runs the proposed plan past a separate reviewer before you hit accept. Cheap insurance on long autonomous runs, and structurally the same builder/critic separation that gauntlet-loop applies to output - here applied to intent instead.

tail.title: selvedge - an append-only log of everything your agent already rejected
tail.summary: Records the approaches an agent considered and discarded, so the next session does not cheerfully re-propose the thing you already ruled out. This is the failure mode that eats the most time across long-running projects with context resets, and an append-only rejection log is a much cheaper fix than full session memory.

tail.title: llmem - local persistent memory for coding agents with no embeddings at all
tail.summary: Deliberately skips the embedding model entirely and keeps memory in a form you can read and grep. Given how broken the embedding caches are on this machine - the fastembed symlink saga - a memory layer with no embedder is worth a serious look rather than a passing one.

tail.title: check-github-status - a skill that stops agents retry-looping through a GitHub outage
tail.summary: Published the same week GitHub Actions had its second-longest major outage: a tiny skill that checks githubstatus.com before the agent burns twenty minutes and a lot of tokens retrying pushes against a service that is down. The general pattern - check the dependency's status page before retrying - is worth generalising to any external API your pipelines hammer.

tail.title: DemoDay - a Claude Code plugin that records demo videos of your own projects
tail.summary: Points the agent at your project and has it produce a walkthrough video rather than a README section. Useful for the parts of your portfolio that are pipelines - a 90-second recording of the NewsBrief run does more for a grant reviewer than a repo tree.

tail.title: animated-voiceover - scripted, voice-consistent animated video from the CLI
tail.summary: A skill for producing animated voiceover videos with reusable scripting, explicit visual direction and voice consistency across segments, all driven from the command line. The voice-consistency handling is the piece worth reading against your Kokoro pipeline, which currently has no notion of a persistent character voice across a long render.

tail.title: pireel - an open-source CapCut alternative that any agent can drive over MCP
tail.summary: A video editor built so the timeline is addressable by an agent rather than only a mouse. Combined with a local TTS pipeline and a local image or video model, this is the missing middle layer between 'Claude wrote the script' and 'here is a finished cut', without a subscription or an upload.

tail.title: open-ai-canvas - an infinite canvas workbench for AI film-making with storyboarding and agent workflows
tail.summary: Multimodal generation, shot sequencing, asset management and agent workflows on one infinite canvas, aimed at film and video creation rather than single-image prompting. The storyboard-as-first-class-object model is the interesting design decision, and it maps onto scene planning for prose as easily as for video.

tail.title: clone-chat - clone someone's texting style from real chat history, entirely locally
tail.summary: Import a real chat log and a local LLM learns the person's tone, emoji habits and reply rhythm, then continues the conversation in character with voice, proactive messages and long-term memory - data never leaves the machine. It is the uncomfortable sibling of mimesis: same corpus-to-voice mechanism, pointed at a specific living person instead of an author's published work, with none of the fingerprint gating. Worth reading precisely for where it declines to put guardrails.

tail.title: shieldfont - a typeface designed to poison unauthorised AI training data
tail.summary: A font whose glyph design is intended to corrupt text scraped from rendered documents while staying legible to humans. Whether it works at scale is very much an open question, and that is the interesting part - it is a testable claim about OCR and scraping pipelines that nobody has actually audited.

tail.title: reflection-engine - a prompt that turns your assistant's memory of you into a candid portrait
tail.summary: A downloadable prompt that asks the model to assemble everything it has stored about you into an evidence-grounded character sketch, citing the specific memories behind each claim rather than flattering you. You have a far richer substrate for this than most people - LKHS plus auto-memory plus two years of transcripts - and the evidence-citation requirement is what would make the output worth reading rather than horoscope.

tail.title: hbg-classical-poem-silk-video - Chinese classical poems rendered as vertical art films with calligraphy captions
tail.summary: An agent skill that takes a classical poem and produces a finished vertical video: generated stills in silk-painting style, a Dockerised image-to-video pass, calligraphy captions, retained ambient sound and scored BGM. The end-to-end orchestration of five different generative steps from a single text input is the transferable part, whatever you think of the output genre.

tail.title: lecture-to-notes - a local GPU pipeline turning recordings into grounded notes and a synced HTML viewer
tail.summary: Whisper via faster-whisper for transcription, minicpm-v:8b through ollama for slide semantics, optional Surya OCR, then alignment of slides to spoken words - all on 8 GB of VRAM, with the GPU stages serialised because Whisper and the VLM cannot share the card. Outputs a self-contained HTML viewer with video, timestamped transcript and summary side by side, plus Obsidian-ready Markdown. Your 5060 Ti has twice the tested VRAM, and this is the shape your audio-overview stack does not yet cover: input rather than output.

tail.title: doc7 - turn documents into AI-ready Markdown with actual visual understanding
tail.summary: A Go tool that converts documents to Markdown using a vision model rather than a text extractor, so figures, tables and layout survive the trip. Given that the Tokenpocalypse story this week traced enterprise AI spend partly to naive PDF-to-markdown conversion, the useful framing is: this is the step you want done well once and locally, not repeatedly through a frontier model.

tail.title: ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3-Easy - one compact workflow for text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last frame and reference video
tail.summary: Collapses the whole MiniMax H3 surface into a single ComfyUI graph with a unified multi-media input: no image connected gives text-to-video, one image gives image-to-video, two gives first/last frame, and reference mode takes up to nine images, three videos and three audio clips. The loader recognises BF16, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, NF4 and GGUF filename variants, which matters on 16 GB where the quantisation choice is the whole ballgame. MIT, drop into custom_nodes.

tail.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit - real-time open-ended video editing with autoregressive diffusion
tail.summary: A 16B multimodal diffusion transformer with an MLLM condition encoder and a causal video VAE that edits frames causally as they arrive, without waiting for the full clip or a fixed length - 30.19 FPS at 720x1280. Handles subject edits, local edits, background swaps, style transfer, motion changes and reference-guided edits from natural language. Apache 2.0, conda + checkpoints from Hugging Face, server at localhost:8080.

tail.title: OmniVAE - an audio-video VAE with cross-modal alignment for joint generation
tail.summary: From OpenMOSS: a single latent space that encodes audio and video together with explicit cross-modal alignment, aimed at joint generation rather than generating video and dubbing it afterwards. The component that everything downstream of MiniMax H3's synchronised-audio results will be built on, and it is open enough to inspect.

tail.title: LeapTalk - stable real-time talking-head video in a single forward step, at arbitrary length
tail.summary: One forward pass per frame with no iterative denoising, which is what makes it real-time and what makes it scale to arbitrarily long videos instead of the usual few-second ceiling. Combined with a local TTS voice, this is the piece that turns a written brief into a talking presenter entirely offline.

tail.title: VideoCoCo - code-as-chain-of-thought for physically consistent video generation
tail.summary: An agentic dual-engine system that has the model write executable code describing the physics of a scene, then generates video conditioned on it - attacking the specific failure where generated video looks right frame by frame and violates conservation of everything across a shot. An unusually inspectable approach to a problem usually addressed by scaling.

tail.title: qwen-audio-agent - a real-time voice runtime that keeps agents talking while they work
tail.summary: A runtime built for the specific problem of an agent that has to stay conversationally present while a long tool call runs, rather than going silent for ninety seconds. Directly comparable to what your conversate skill does with local whisper plus Kokoro, and worth reading for how it handles the interruption and barge-in cases.

tail.title: claude-thing - a Spotify Car Thing reborn as a hardware Claude Code HUD
tail.summary: An extension of the Nocturne firmware project that turns Spotify's discontinued and now nearly free Car Thing into a dedicated always-on display for Claude Code session state. The genre - abandoned consumer hardware repurposed as an agent status panel - is one of the more appealing corners of this whole ecosystem, and the device costs almost nothing second-hand.

tail.title: echolocal - a complete local replacement for an Echo Dot, wired to Home Assistant
tail.summary: Go, runs on your own hardware, speaks to Home Assistant, and replaces a second-generation Echo Dot end to end with nothing leaving the house. The reference build for the local-voice-assistant question, and it pairs naturally with a Kokoro-class TTS you already run.

tail.title: Sidebar - a private ESP32 intercom for five kids, no accounts, no cloud
tail.summary: A parent built a household push-to-talk network on ESP32 boards - no accounts, no service, no company that can shut it off - and wrote it up properly with the design decisions and the failures. The best kind of hardware post: small scope, real constraints, honest about what did not work.

tail.title: Rodeo - a robot that earns its own electricity
tail.summary: A research-lab robot built around an energy budget it has to satisfy by its own actions, which turns power into a first-class constraint on the policy rather than an assumption. Strange, small, and a much more interesting framing of autonomy than the usual task-completion benchmark.

tail.title: Lefts - a domain-specific language for building creative ML models
